structured_output.text: I could not solve this. The statement is the Erdős–Turán conjecture for additive bases of order 2 (Erdős problem listed with a $500 prize): if A+A contains all large integers, is the representation function unbounded? The expected answer is yes, but it is open as far as I know. I did not find a proof or a counterexample. Known: Erdős constructed bases with representation function ≍ log n; Ruzsa constructed bases with bounded mean-square representation function; bounded-representation bases are not ruled out in general. Simple counting gives only A(N) ≍ sqrt(N) if the representation function were bounded, and generating-function arguments with f(z)^2 = 1/(1-z) + bounded-coefficient terms give no contradiction from the real axis alone. So I report no resolution.
